cultural.vision_reason: A strip-woven cotton textile with dark blue ground, supplementary-weft geometric patterning, and metallic tinsel wefts — a handwoven narrow-strip cloth consistent with Guinea-Bissau/Senegambian weaving traditions, plausibly Papel-made.

physical.title: textile
physical.summary:
Textile consisting of six narrow strip woven cotton lengths, hand sewn together selvedge to selvedge. Ground weave: plain weave: dyed blue cotton warps and dyed blue and white cotton wefts. There are also a number of silver tinsel wefts thorughout the cloth.  This creates a cloth with a dark blue background with bands of weft stripes at either end in white with a silver 'sparkle.' The cloth is then decorated using supplementary weft and supplementary weft floats in white. There is a band of white check at each end of the cloth flanked by the white stripes mentioned earlier. The central panel consists of six warp stripes which are decorated with chains of diamonds consisting of warp lines. These diamonds are backed by black and white check bordered by white warp stripes. There is, throughout the whole cloth, a sprinkling of sparkle created by the small amounts of tinsel woven into the cloth.

The textile is finished in unworked warps.
